characters.description: A Refined defender of Alefast whose command of iron and void is joined to broad magical perception. Her new soulbond with Kit lets her control the sanctum's openings and transfer surplus power into it.
characters.name: Tala

characters.description: A distinct collaborator who shares Tala's body and assists her thinking and research. Their unusual partnership predates the events of this volume and gives Tala another perspective within their shared existence.
characters.name: Alat

characters.description: Tala's living dimensional refuge and newly soulbound companion. The bond has advanced Kit to Refined power, repaired its damaged magic, and given it the ability to accept Tala's excess power while its travel systems are improved.
characters.name: Kit

characters.description: Tala's kinetic-mage friend and a former apprentice of Grediv. He trains with Tala and Cazor, developing tactics and equipment intended to overcome the advantages of iron magic while maintaining his place in Tala's close circle.
characters.name: Rain

characters.description: Tala's flicker-teleporting flockmate and trusted combat partner. His ability to pass through even a minute opening into Kit makes him well suited to testing the sanctum's newly controlled entrances and their practical limits.
characters.name: Terry

characters.description: An Alefast Paragon who leads defenders, watches over Rain, and oversees the training around Tala. He is an established authority within the circle handling Alefast's external threats and the development of its defenders.
characters.name: Grediv

characters.description: An iron specialist who spars with Tala and Rain and provides a practical test for Rain's experimental counters to iron magic, including tactics built around magical monopoles.
characters.name: Cazor

characters.description: Banfast's City Stone holder, head of its Archon Council, and a Paragon specializing in soulbonds involving dimensional storage. She evaluates Kit's new bond and begins work on reliable teleportation access.
characters.name: Elnia

characters.description: A fox-like arcane exile who deals in artifacts and arcane goods while concealed by a human illusion. He holds credit owed to Tala through Ingrit and takes a commercial interest in Kit's unusual nature.
characters.name: Lisa

characters.description: Tala's dying mentor, whose condition is failing as she resists the formation of an Archon star.
characters.name: Odara

characters.description: A constructionist and one of Kit's resident co-operators. He works with Elnia's staff to establish incoming and outgoing teleportation for the newly soulbound sanctum while helping assess how its expanded capabilities should be used.
characters.name: Simon

characters.description: A member of Kit's established household who lives and works there alongside Simon. Her cooperation in maintaining the unusual dimensional home predates this volume and makes her one of its continuing resident partners.
characters.name: Petra

characters.description: A gateless researcher who studies artifacts and magical harvests with his family. He is Brandon's father, and neither man can use the gate-based magic available to most humans. His wife directs their family business.
characters.name: Adrill

characters.description: Adrill's gateless son, who has inherited his father's inability to use human gate magic.
characters.name: Brandon

characters.description: Adrill's wife and a gated artifact worker whose family has been disrupted by Adrill's accidental magical change. She asks Tala for a path to enough advancement to preserve a shared future with him instead of accepting a new difference in their lifespans.
characters.name: Brandon's mother

characters.description: Simon and Petra's elder daughter, an academy graduate with healing talent who plans to seek a healer's apprenticeship.
characters.name: Simon and Petra's elder daughter

characters.description: Brandon's mother, who assists Kedva immediately after her magical transformation.
characters.name: Artia

characters.description: Simon and Petra's elder daughter, who knew Tala at the academy and is now training as a healer under Mistress Vanga. She has obtained healing inscriptions.
characters.name: Anna

characters.description: Brandon's partner, whom he hopes might be able to share the life-extending change forced upon him. Her connection to him makes the consequences of his transformation immediately personal and raises the question of whether she could safely follow him.
characters.name: Kedva

characters.description: A visitor who arrives to advise Adrill, Brandon, and Kedva about their magical condition.
characters.name: Nadro

characters.description: A stone mage in Tala's defender unit and a widower still processing his wife's death. Tala seeks his counsel while grieving her own recent loss, recognizing that his experience may offer a healthier way to carry enduring grief.
characters.name: Gert

characters.description: A censured member of the House of Blood who grieves its last heir. After carrying out an unauthorized purge of the House's opponents, she broadcasts a private mourning song strengthened by magic across Platoirie on the anniversary of the heir's death.
characters.name: Mia Lane

characters.description: A dwarf who leads a growing underground settlement open to varied inhabitants. He alone can wield the concept sword Tala gave him, and expeditions to ruins have obtained durable magical power sources for his community.
characters.name: Thrawn

characters.description: The keeper of several mushroom-linked creatures, including Kevin. She investigates the forced Doskanok bond associated with Tala but decides that reproducing it would require conditions too dangerous and uncertain to attempt.
characters.name: Noelle

characters.description: Tala's soulbound weapon, able to change its physical form. Flo is an established part of her equipment and a participant in her combat partnership, combining a personal bond with the practical flexibility of a morphic weapon.
characters.name: Flo

characters.description: A void-and-kinetic mage hunter who restrains Kedva after mistaking her for an arcane. Once her registration is verified, he apologizes, recommends certified identification for her, and agrees to discuss void magic with Tala.
characters.name: Tai

characters.description: Tala's established information-broker liaison. She manages information and credit connected to Tala, providing an ongoing point of contact for arrangements that depend on knowledge, negotiation, and obligations carried between interested parties.
characters.name: Ingrit

characters.description: The principal modern maker of containment-cell cores. His design anchors cells from the Doman Emeth and derives from older cores first made by the people who later became the Leshkin, placing his work behind current containment practice.
characters.name: Jevin

characters.description: Tala's younger sister. She turns down magical advancement and academy enrollment in favor of an ordinary life.
characters.name: Nia

characters.description: An Archon who shares responsibility for the Jasmine Dragon tea shop with his nephew Okus. As Iazo's elder brother, he encourages Okus to avoid his father's damaging pursuit of power. He tells Rain that stopping refinement is a valid choice that can later be reconsidered.
characters.name: Ori

characters.description: The deceased fire mage who became a fount. He was Ori's younger brother and Okus's father, and he died holding a photograph of his family.
characters.name: Iazo

characters.description: An ancient reality mage confined in a deteriorating containment cell. Her gate suppresses magic and void, and she has erased her original name from ordinary reality records.
characters.name: the reality prisoner

characters.description: An exceptionally powerful reforged mage assigned as backup for the mission against the reality prisoner. He prepares tailored natural magic but expects the less advanced defenders to solve whatever lies within their abilities.
characters.name: the reforged mage

characters.description: The giant-wolf pack's young Refined combatant, chosen to test Tala under formal rules. It faces Tala and Terry in a duel where ordinary inscriptions are disabled and the outcome must be surrender or death.
characters.name: the young giant wolf

recaps.ending: Tala ends the reality prisoner's threat by restoring the identity and death the prisoner had denied. The reforged mage helps balance the released reality power, and Kit absorbs the stabilized cell. Tala and Terry then survive the giant-wolf trial, and Tala's victory earns only an opening toward future cooperation with the pack. The slain young wolf is restored by its god-beast and directed to consider Tala a possible ally. Rain has survived three refining sessions but remains fused after pausing before another. He finds a purpose in protecting people and begins courting Tala, who is not ready for marriage. Terry is healed and privately weighs a soulbond with Tala without committing to it. Brandon and Kedva are married, soulbound, expecting a son, and settled in Irondale, where Brandon works with Simon. Kit now contains a growing community and two recovered cells, but its exceptional magical density and dormant automaton require control. The sleeping city, hostile Doman Emeth entities, regional cell failures, Rain's refinement, wolf relations, and possible outside awareness of Tala's devourer nature remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: After soulbonding Kit, Tala makes the sanctum safer but accidentally gives Adrill and Brandon durable natural magic. Kedva freely accepts a dangerous version of the same change, while Tala wrestles with consent, mortality, and her path toward Paragon. Rain survives three traumatic refining sessions and pauses before a fourth. Tala recovers a containment core from the Doman Emeth, turns Kit's expanded space into Irondale, and nearly creates self-propagating ice. Brandon and Kedva marry, soulbond, and prepare for a child. Tala later destroys an ancient reality prisoner by restoring the identity and death the prisoner denied, then absorbs the balanced cell into Kit. In a giant-wolf trial, Tala and Terry defeat a young wolf at severe cost. The wolf is later restored by its god-beast, leaving cautious cooperation possible. Tala and Rain begin courting, while Terry considers a soulbond and an outside threat may have noticed Tala's devourer resonance.

recaps.text: Previously: Tala entered this volume as a Refined defender of Alefast with command of iron and void. She shares her body with Alat, a distinct inner collaborator who supports her thinking and research. Terry is her flicker-teleporting flockmate and combat partner, while Flo is her soulbound, shape-changing weapon. Kit is a living dimensional refuge used by Tala's household, including Simon and Petra, and Tala has been working toward a soulbond with it. Rain is Tala's kinetic-mage friend and a former apprentice of the Paragon Grediv. Cazor trains with them as an iron specialist. Ingrit manages information and credit connected to Tala. These relationships place Tala at the center of both Alefast's defense and a growing household whose safety depends on the unusual powers surrounding Kit. Her established responsibilities therefore join public defense, personal advancement, and the care of companions whose lives are increasingly tied to her choices.

Tala completes her soulbond with Kit, repairing and advancing the living sanctum while gaining control over its openings and a place to send excess power. Elnia confirms that visitors can enter without being forced into a bond and begins teleportation work with Simon. After training with Rain and Cazor, Tala's improved perception reveals human gates and other intrusive detail she must learn to manage. In Banfast, the arcane dealer Lisa offers a purifier for Kit. Tala trades a combat memory for it, then learns that her dying mentor has disappeared and later died. Once integrated, the purifier fills Kit with dense, unbound natural magic. That environment overwhelms the gateless researchers Adrill and Brandon. To save them, Tala forms natural magical pathways in their bodies, giving them basic magical perception and cognitive enhancement. The intervention succeeds medically but changes their lives without consent. Kit is now safer for ordinary contents yet dangerous to unprepared people, and Tala must address the consequences for the two men and their families.

Adrill and Brandon's new natural magic may greatly extend their lives, leaving Tala burdened by the change she imposed while saving them. Grediv confirms that they remain human and explains that their abilities depend on dense ambient magic. Adrill's wife asks Tala for help pursuing enough advancement to share his longer future. Brandon's betrothed, Kedva, independently asks for the same transformation and accepts its risk. Tala restricts access to Kit and prepares carefully, while her emerging Paragon purpose shifts toward helping people pursue freely chosen goals. She also begins processing her mentor's death with Gert, Rain, and Simon and Petra's returning daughter. Kedva reaffirms her choice before her family and enters Kit for the procedure. Tala releases the sanctum's full density, controls the dangerous absorption, and uses prepared material as a template for new natural magic. She discovers that her authority inside Kit could control Kedva's body almost completely, rejects any claim of ownership, and continues only because stopping would endanger Kedva. By the end of the chapter, the irreversible remaking is still underway and its outcome is not yet known.

Kedva survives her transformation and emerges as a gateless human using arcane-style natural magic. Her strength and resilience are considerable in Kit but decline outside its dense power, so Tala and Rain begin training her. A highly advanced gateless adviser establishes retention and release exercises for Kedva, Adrill, and Brandon. He also warns that Kit could grant extraordinary longevity to trained residents, making its true value dangerous if powerful houses learn of it. Tala's grief eases as she discusses mortality and her mentor, while Gert demonstrates both his stone magic and his own way of living with loss. Wider interludes show other communities and powerful individuals responding to past events. Rain then begins a planned series of refinement sessions. The first process repeatedly damages and rebuilds his body, triggering uncontrolled kinetic blades. Tala enters the chamber, withstands the attacks, and helps redirect his unconscious focus until they stop. Rain survives but requires intensive recovery. Grediv admits that some candidates cannot finish refinement, and Tala forces him to withdraw a threat made while arranging for her to receive information Rain may not be told.

While Rain struggles to recover from his first refinement, Tala's unit enters a doomsday vault cell containing resources for rebuilding civilization. To retrieve its core, Tala opens a route into the Doman Emeth. Hostile entities there can invert her magic and erase parts of her magic-dependent existence. Kit consumes the vault, but Tala loses her lower body while extracting the core and must sever the damaged boundary so she can regenerate. She is removed from duty while healing. Kedva's arcane-like power later causes Tai, a void-and-kinetic mage hunter, to mistake her for an arcane, though official registration resolves the confrontation. Tai then exchanges magical theory with Tala and Rain. He identifies void as a boundary and finds an unused element in Flo's magic. Tala's attempt to add a reality component cracks the soulbound weapon, but she repairs it and suspends further reckless experimentation. Study with Kit deepens her command of void. Rain's assessment finds him about three-quarters of the way to Refined after one session and gives him a viable, though uncertain, chance of completing the process. The intensity and timing of future sessions remain his choice.

Tala separates Kit's newly acquired surplus space into Irondale, a settlement meant to house residents and provide resources she truly owns for eventual reforging. Her defender unit also seals a cell containing an entire city under a contagious sleeping curse, leaving its people alive but without a trusted cure. A wider interlude shows competing approaches to power and protection, including Jevin's dangerous attempt to reforge his own body. In Kit, Tala compresses water into an unfamiliar ice that converts further water into itself. It begins growing inside Simon, forcing Tala to remove the affected material before a healer restores his arm. The group destroys the ice and halts water-based siege experiments. Rain completes a second maximum-intensity refinement while Tala protects herself from his uncontrolled kinetic attacks. He remains unconscious for nine days, then wakes with lingering psychological trauma. Tala discovers new ways to move Kit's local manifestation and bring people inside. After a month, Rain is physically recovered and his projected chance of eventual success improves, but another session is delayed. Simon and Petra ask whether seeking refinement is worth the risk, and Tala still lacks a settled answer about longevity or eternity.

Rain completes a third refining session but suffers severe panic and trauma afterward. Tala remains with him through the immediate crisis, then supports his recovery as they defeat a siphon infiltration outside Alefast. Irondale develops into a low-magic community suitable for gateless families. Brandon and Kedva marry there, form a soulbond, and learn that Kedva is pregnant. Brandon later becomes Simon's full-time assistant, and the couple settles permanently at Irondale's edge while Kedva limits her magic for the pregnancy. Rain eventually tells Tala that he cannot face the final refinement and fears being left behind. Tala's family conversations make her reconsider her hopes for partnership and children without forcing a decision. Her younger sister chooses an ordinary life instead of magical advancement, and an experienced Archon tells Rain that stopping is a valid choice he may revisit. Back in Alefast, Tala merges reality nodes in a sparring space. The resulting region greatly resists ordinary magic while remaining easier for Tala and Terry to navigate. Grediv identifies it as a conceptual working, opening a new area of research just as Tala prepares to dismiss it safely.

Tala stabilizes the altered space in Kit, then joins a mission against an ancient reality mage in a failing containment cell. The prisoner's gate suppresses magic and void, and her identity depends on rejecting her original name and death. Tala enters without Terry and refuses the prisoner's offer to eliminate gates. Their confrontation clarifies Tala's emerging purpose as a defender of gated humanity and a nurturer of magic. After losing an arm to direct reality erasure, Tala retrieves the prisoner's forgotten name from the archive and repeatedly restores the identity the woman denied. The prisoner's conceptual working breaks, her whole soul briefly returns, and she rejects passage onward before fading. Her accumulated reality power remains hazardous. A reforged backup mage channels immense natural magic through Tala's aura to balance it, while teaching her how reality, magic, and void constrain one another. Three days later, Kit consumes the stabilized cell and Tala begins replenishing the enlarged sanctum's power. She returns to Alefast and relies on Rain's quiet friendship while processing the mission. The dormant automaton in Kit remains unsafe to activate autonomously because soulless constructs are vulnerable to reality corruption.

More than two hundred people move into Irondale under controlled access and Tala's declared authority. A giant-wolf pack then arrives to test young Refined humans as a possible first step toward closer relations. Tala is the only eligible fighter present, and Terry joins as her recognized flockmate while Rain's fused state excludes him. With ordinary inscriptions disabled, Tala and Terry face a young wolf in a duel ending only in surrender or death. The wolf's speed, void attacks, healing, and subtle mental influence nearly overwhelm them. Terry wounds it with Flo but is badly hurt and withdraws on Tala's order. The wolf tears off Tala's left arm and leg, yet her accumulating claim over its iron steadily weakens it and finally kills it. Tala reattaches her limbs after her inscriptions return and consumes the body to recover. The pack grants limited acknowledgment, not an alliance. Rain identifies protecting people as his reason to continue advancing, and he and Tala begin courting without an engagement. The wolf's god-beast later restores it and directs it to learn from the loss. The wolf kills an outside observer that intended to report Tala's devourer resonance, though whether any warning escaped is unknown. Terry heals and privately considers, but does not accept, a soulbond with Tala.

characters.description: Brightsong's founder and council leader. He begins the book badly injured after defeating two dragons, unable to contact Besal, and troubled that the resulting oath has placed both dragons under his control.
characters.name: Hal

characters.name: Besal

characters.description: Hal's romantic partner and a leader on Brightsong's council.
characters.name: Noth

characters.name: Ashera

characters.description: Hal's mimic familiar and a member of Brightsong's council. Vorax serves as a trusted companion within the settlement's leadership circle.
characters.name: Vorax

characters.description: Hal's close protector, described as his koblin shadow. Lurklox remains near him as Brightsong prepares for further danger.
characters.name: Lurklox

characters.description: A fire-aligned dragon who can assume human form. Hal's recent victory has bound him by an oath.
characters.name: Gold dragon

characters.description: An ice-aligned dragon who can take human form. Newly subject to Hal through the dragon oath, she openly describes the arrangement as enslavement.
characters.name: Tyrant white dragon

characters.description: A childlike figure who becomes distressed during the meeting about the dragon oath and leaves.
characters.name: Childlike oracle

characters.description: A disguised adult elf-like figure who binds Besal to secrecy after assuring him that her proposal will not directly endanger Hal. She offers to find his weakened form a sturdier vessel.
characters.name: Oracle-like helper

characters.description: Ashera's familiar and the intended user of a commissioned mithril frying pan.
characters.name: Ashera's Appa familiar

characters.description: A dwarf artisan hired by Ashera to forge cookware from mithril. Payment for the work includes the use of dragonfire.
characters.name: Dwarf goldsmith

characters.description: A hostile founder whom Hal believes may be an alternate version of himself. Rinbast controls other alternate selves and stands behind the Kinslayer threat facing Brightsong.
characters.name: Rinbast

characters.description: A powerful drow operative who takes charge of the weakened Besal in the unstable Fathomways. She subjects him to dangerous tests while keeping her larger purpose concealed.
characters.name: Drow assassin

characters.description: An independent founder travelling under a false identity with the hidden Kinslayer expedition. She considers turning against its increasingly unstable archmage but does not know whether Hal would accept her help.
characters.name: Undercover founder

characters.description: A tribal scout guiding the concealed expedition near Brightsong. His knowledge of the region helps the party remain hidden while Hal's patrols search for it.
characters.name: Poisonheart scout

characters.description: The unstable leader of the hidden expedition near Brightsong. He serves Rinbast, cannot penetrate the settlement's anti-magic barrier, and is becoming harder for his own companions to trust.
characters.name: Tower archmage

characters.description: A Brightsong ally who joins Angram in assessing an unexpected tower mage while Hal is unconscious.
characters.name: Mira

characters.description: A Brightsong ranger ally who works with Mira to question the newly arrived tower mage and determine whether he poses a danger to the settlement.
characters.name: Angram

characters.description: A noncombatant mage brought toward Brightsong with urgent news. He admits relying on stolen travel scrolls while his abilities and loyalties remain under scrutiny.
characters.name: Tower mage

characters.description: The tower mage identifies himself as a food mage after demonstrating magic that produces hardy, edible crops. He asks to remain in Brightsong and continue his research.
characters.name: Food mage

characters.description: A long-time acquaintance of the newly arrived tower mage. Lay brings him toward Brightsong with urgent information and vouches for him while both remain under assessment.
characters.name: Lay

characters.description: Brightsong's resident brewing creature. When the town hall and its equipment undergo an unexplained transformation, the innkeeper denies causing the change.
characters.name: Appa innkeeper

characters.description: A critically weakened female Kinslayer who arrives at Brightsong seeking asylum. Hal recognizes her connection to Besal's apparent death and initially responds as if she remains an enemy.
characters.name: Female Kinslayer

characters.description: The second Kinslayer seeking refuge at Brightsong after breaking from Rinbast. Like the wounded woman beside him, he is an alternate version of Hal whose intentions have not yet been proven.
characters.name: Second Kinslayer

characters.name: Lamora

characters.name: Val

characters.name: Barden

characters.name: Dale

characters.name: Elora

characters.description: A weakened dwarf council member whose missing soul fragment may be recoverable through a dungeon expedition.
characters.name: Durvin

characters.description: Barden's son, weakened after losing a soul fragment during the return to Aldim.
characters.name: Barden's son

characters.description: Brightsong's Appa innkeeper is the familiar for whom Ashera commissioned a mithril cooking implement. The innkeeper needs it to improve the inn's food.
characters.name: Appa innkeeper

recaps.ending: Brightsong reaches winter with shelter, food, stronger defenses, working smithing, and controlled magical farms. Hal has replaced the dragons' coercive oath with a reciprocal alliance, cured his founder-mark injury, removed his hollow essence, restored Durvin's soul fragment, and gained a legendary fused crafting class. Besal remains alive and independent in the Fathomways, pursuing allies against eldritch threats. Val and the Poisonheart scout survive their stand against the tower archmage, though the scout loses an arm and is likely blinded in one eye. Hal kills the archmage with the mage's stored disintegration spell, preserves Val's body, and reaches her lost consciousness. The captured mobile archspire is sealed pending inspection. Rinbast remains protected from direct conflict outside the Primacy Trials, Durvin's claim to the Anvil is unresolved, and another dwarf soul fragment still awaits recovery. Aldim may need to ascend to survive, but ascension could expose it to forces that consume world shards. Hal privately decides to return to the Abyss and has not told Noth his true purpose.
recaps.in_short: After defeating two dragons, Hal refuses to keep them enslaved by their oath and negotiates a reciprocal alliance that grants him dragonfire. Besal survives their separation, becomes physically independent, and takes up an anti-eldritch mission. Hal cures his founder-mark injury, turns defecting Kinslayers and an undercover founder into oath-bound allies, restores Durvin's missing soul fragment, and sheds the hollow essence restricting his powers. Brightsong gains homes, metalworking, magical crops, controlled monster farms, and Hal's legendary fused crafting. Mira reveals that Aldim is a declining world shard whose ascension could attract shard-consuming enemies. Val draws the returning tower archmage away from Hal and nearly dies beside the Poisonheart scout. Hal kills the archmage with his own captured spell, saves both defenders, recovers Val's consciousness, and claims the mobile archspire. Brightsong enters winter secure, while Besal continues his separate mission, Rinbast remains beyond direct reach, and Hal secretly prepares to return to the Abyss.

recaps.text: Previously: Hal founded Brightsong in the Shiverglades and leads its council with Noth, his partner. Ashera serves as his envoy, Vorax is his mimic familiar, and Lurklox protects him. Hal is a Beastborn and an Oathforger whose powers are linked to Besal, his inner counterpart.

Hal wakes to learn that victory over a gold dragon and a tyrant white dragon has made both obey him under the White Gold Oath. He rejects the result and refuses exchanges that would free them by stripping away their power. While Brightsong searches for approaching Kinslayers, Hal chooses the Founder leadership path because it best supports his duty to protect the settlement. Besal is alive in the Fathomways but weak, separate from Hal, and bound by secrecy to an oracle-like helper who offers him a temporary vessel. Ashera secretly locates mithril for a crafting project, keeping the seam concealed because of the danger it could attract. Hal finally negotiates an equivalent replacement for the dragons' servitude. They give him dragonfire and agree to train him, while he recognizes the white dragon's territorial rights under Brightsong's authority and accepts reciprocal restrictions on using the flame. Both dragons approve the revised oath, ending their slave-like condition, and Hal survives the transfer of gold and white dragonfire.

Besal travels through the unstable Fathomways under the control of a powerful drow ritualist. When an eldritch creature shatters the stones sustaining him, he consumes it so completely that it cannot return. The oracle-like helper saves him and shows him disastrous possible futures for Hal, Brightsong, and Aldim, arguing that limited intervention is necessary. Meanwhile, Hal learns to channel gold dragonfire through hope and white dragonfire through patience and controlled use of ambient aether. Training turns his hostility with the white dragon toward mutual respect, and he commits to a deeper Draconic Vow with both dragons. Besal then chooses an independent existence. A concealed ritual uses an eldritch captive to sever his remaining bonds, temporarily clearing Hal's accumulated strain and corruption. Besal gains a physical body and the unique Star Scourge class. He remains committed to protecting Hal and Aldim, but decides to secure equipment and strength before returning as an equal rather than resuming his former place inside Hal.

A hidden Kinslayer expedition waits near Brightsong, blocked by the settlement's anti-magic barrier. Its undercover founder considers defecting from the unstable tower archmage and offers the two injured Kinslayers a way out. In Brightsong, Hal collapses when Besal's final bond is severed, then wakes with his strain symptoms gone. A newly arrived noncombatant food mage demonstrates magic that can create hardy, productive crops and asks to join the settlement. Hal still suffers dangerous founder-mark bleed, so the gold and white dragons combine their flames while he uses Draconic Purity. The ritual cures him and produces a call recognized across the Shiverglades as a prophecy of the Bright King. The Poisonheart scout abandons the archmage, the undercover founder flees with the Kinslayers, and political powers begin reacting. Hal assimilates a copper founder mark, starts a new quest, and uses temporarily free sigils to carve homes and defenses into the mountains. His sigil use no longer causes the disabling pain that had threatened his life.

The tower archmage breaches Brightsong and attacks Hal with a destructive spell. Hal captures it with his sigils, defeats the mage's defenses, and forces him to escape, although revival magic prevents a permanent victory. Soon afterward, the undercover founder arrives with two defecting Kinslayers, Lamora, and the Poisonheart scout. The wounded female Kinslayer is an alternate version of Hal whose beast has died, and Hal stabilizes her through Dominate while retaining the tether as a safeguard. The undercover founder offers an alliance against Rinbast and instruction in using Magisite to fuel founder marks. After debate, Hal grants conditional sanctuary. The newcomers join the Bravers Guild and swear the Oath of the Bright King, which bars deliberate harm to allies and obliges them to protect incapacitated companions. Hal earns rewards for turning enemies into allies and begins learning Magisite-supported sigil use. The alliance leaves trust unresolved, but Brightsong gains a founder with her own territory, two former Kinslayers, Lamora, and a local scout rather than facing them as an attacking force.

Hal plans for winter while learning to function without Besal. Val, the female Kinslayer, gives him her name and asks him to kill her if strain ever destroys her identity. She keeps his light Dominate connection voluntarily and begins exchanging Beastborn knowledge with him. Ashera brings secretly mined mithril for an innkeeper's quest, while Barden organizes the smithy effort. Hal uses dragonfire and copper sigils to produce high-purity iron and enough mithril for the project. He then enters a soul-fragment dungeon with Mira, Vorax, and the weakened Durvin. The dungeon forces Durvin through traumatic memories and reveals him as the dispossessed Steelheart heir to the Anvil. After he overcomes the memory constructs, Hal spares the sentient dungeon core and gives it all of his harmful hollow essence. The core returns Durvin's missing soul fragment. Hal leaves with his locked monster essences restored, a soul bond with Vorax that preserves the familiar's independence, and access to costly travel through the Fathomways. Durvin is whole again, but his future claim to the Anvil remains unsettled.

With his essences available again, Hal collaborates with the food mage on mana batteries, conduits, and a farm grid. The system accelerates crops, but excess mana also produces plant monsters. Hal develops anchors that concentrate the spawns and establishes strict limits after an overgrown cycle overwhelms its guards. The resulting farms can provide food, combat training, and experience if Brightsong controls each harvest carefully. The settlement's smithy and sawmill operate, cottages rise, and Noth works with Elora on gateway towers and excavation slimes. Hal's renewed crafting advances into a fusion quest. He sacrifices levels from separate crafts to gain a legendary combined class with greater mana, speed, efficiency, and the ability to work bone and aether together. The quest suggests that such fusions can strengthen Aldim itself. At the same time, strain-driven aggression remains a concern for Hal without Besal's filtering, and the tower archmage is still expected to return.

Besal advances separately, permanently consuming an eldritch guardian while his party seeks an undead lich as a potential ally. In Brightsong, Hal uses his fused craft to create advanced storage vessels, Elder Glass, armor, and a rebuilt soulbound weapon. He plans to train with Val after another dwarf soul-fragment expedition. The white dragon gives him rare white aether and requests a southern mountain spur for her nest, but both she and Mira react fearfully when Hal asks about ascending Aldim. During the expedition, Mira finally explains the danger. Aldim is a low-ranked, declining world shard within a larger war against forces that consume worlds. Hal's fusion quests may help it rise, but a shard becomes exposed during ascension, so strengthening Aldim without adequate protection could deliver it to those enemies. Hal now understands that repairing the world is necessary but cannot safely pursue ascension without a broader defense. Outside the dungeon, Val senses danger and remains behind with the Poisonheart scout.

Val discovers that the tower archmage has been tracking her and breaks Hal's Dominate restraint so she can draw the threat away from him. Without her beast, every use of Beastborn strain shortens her prospects and risks erasing her identity. She attacks the archmage alone, driving herself into increasingly severe strain. The Poisonheart scout joins her and wounds the mage, but loses an arm and suffers a grave eye injury. Hal arrives before the archmage can execute Val. He releases the mage's own stored disintegration spell through gold sigils, killing him and claiming his mobile archspire and equipment. Hal stabilizes the scout through their bond, then uses Dominate to keep Val's heart and lungs working while he reaches her lost consciousness. Val wakes in Brightsong under Noth's care, and the scout survives with permanent disabilities. Hal restricts access to the captured archspire until it is safe. Snow arrives with Brightsong housed and provisioned. Besal remains on his independent anti-eldritch mission, Rinbast remains an unresolved threat, and Hal privately decides to return to the Abyss without telling Noth his true reason.

characters.description: A Highland laird in his mid-twenties, left wounded and half-conscious on the field at Culloden with a shattered leg and no wish to survive. He has spent two years trying to prevent the rising and has lost everything to it, including the wife he sent back through the standing stones. Stubborn, honourable, and quietly formidable even in ruin, he expects to be shot with the rest of the Jacobite wounded.
characters.name: Jamie Fraser

characters.description: The English dragoon captain who tormented Jamie and Claire for years. He fought at Culloden and died there, and Jamie's last clear memory of the battle is of the two of them meeting on the field. His marriage to Mary Hawkins, made to give his dying brother's child a name, is what secures the family line that leads to Frank Randall.
characters.name: Jonathan Randall

characters.description: Returned to 1948 through the stones and pregnant with Jamie's child, a woman with no way back and a husband waiting for her who has spent three years believing her lost. Practical and stubborn, she sets about building a life she did not choose, and in time trains as a physician in Boston. Twenty years later, in 1968, she is a surgeon, a widow, and the mother of a grown daughter.
characters.name: Claire Randall

characters.description: Claire's first husband, a Cambridge historian who takes her back after her three-year disappearance and agrees to raise another man's child as his own. Decent, wounded, and proud, he sets conditions: the past is never discussed, and Claire never searches for Jamie Fraser again.
characters.name: Frank Randall

characters.description: Jamie's elder sister, who holds Lallybroch together through the years of occupation, redcoat searches, and near-starvation that follow Culloden. Sharp, unsentimental, and quietly ruthless in defence of her family, she manages an estate legally owned by a child and a brother the English are hunting.
characters.name: Jenny Murray

characters.description: Claire's daughter, twenty years old in 1968, tall and red-haired, an engineering student raised in Boston by Frank. She has recently learned the truth about her parentage and is struggling with it, torn between the father who brought her up and a man two centuries dead whom her mother will not stop looking for.
characters.name: Brianna Randall

characters.description: The young historian who first helped Claire trace the men of Lallybroch, now caught up in a much larger search: whether Jamie Fraser can be followed through twenty years of Scottish records. Methodical and patient, he works through prison rolls and ledgers while his interest in Brianna grows.
characters.name: Roger Wakefield

characters.description: An English army officer, young, fair and small of stature, who takes up the governorship of Ardsmuir prison and finds among the Jacobite inmates a man he has met before under humiliating circumstances. Cultured, scrupulous, and lonely, he offers Jamie parole, conversation, and a friendship complicated by feelings he does not expect to have returned.
characters.name: Lord John Grey

characters.description: The elder daughter of the Dunsany family, at whose Lake District estate Jamie is placed as a paroled groom. Wilful, spoiled, and facing a marriage to a rich old man she detests, she discovers who her father's Scottish servant really is and uses it against him.
characters.name: Geneva Dunsany

characters.description: A small boy raised as the heir to an English earldom, imperious, fearless, and devoted to the Scottish groom who teaches him to ride. Jamie is the only person he will obey, and the resemblance between them becomes harder to overlook as the boy grows.
characters.name: Willie

characters.description: The French orphan Jamie took off the Paris streets, now a grown man with one hand missing, living in Edinburgh and helping run Jamie's illicit business. Charming, capable, and wholly loyal, he handles the parts of the trade that need a light touch.
characters.name: Fergus Fraser

characters.description: Jenny's fourteen-year-old son, gangling and rash, who has run away from Lallybroch to find his uncle in Edinburgh and is determined not to be sent home. He is inseparable from his enormous half-wolf dog, Rollo, and has an unerring instinct for being where the trouble is.
characters.name: Young Ian

characters.description: A small Chinese exile living rough in Edinburgh, a scholar and poet in his own country who now survives on Jamie's protection and a good deal of drink. Erudite, exasperating, and largely misunderstood by everyone around him, he has a story he has never been asked to tell.
characters.name: Mr. Willoughby

characters.description: A woman from Jamie's Highland past, once infatuated with him and no friend to Claire, now a widow with two daughters. What she has become to Jamie in the twenty years since Culloden is a fact Claire learns without warning.
characters.name: Laoghaire MacKenzie

characters.description: Laoghaire's elder daughter, a blunt, self-possessed teenager who has decided what she wants from life and is not much troubled by other people's objections to it. She holds Claire responsible for wrecking her mother's marriage.
characters.name: Marsali MacKimmie

characters.description: The Scottish herbalist Claire knew at Cranesmuir, who was condemned as a witch and whom Claire believed dead. She is alive, rich, and settled on a West Indies plantation, still pursuing the Jacobite obsession that took her through the stones in the first place, and still perfectly willing to use people up to get what she wants.
characters.name: Geillis Duncan

recaps.ending: In Jamaica the trail leads to Geillis Duncan, alive under a married name and rich on a sugar plantation. She has been collecting gemstones because they are what a traveller needs to survive the stones, and she means to go forward through a cave called Abandawe to put a Scottish king on the throne, taking Young Ian as the sacrifice she believes the passage requires. Claire follows her into the cave and kills her; Jamie and Ian get out alive. Lord John Grey, now governor of Jamaica, has meanwhile put Jamie's son Willie in front of him again, and Claire has learned who the boy is. Wanted for murder and piracy and unable to stay, the Frasers put to sea, and the ship is destroyed in a hurricane. Claire and Jamie are washed ashore on the coast of Georgia, penniless, alive, and in the American colonies, with Young Ian and a few survivors. They have no way back to Scotland and no wish to go. The book ends with the two of them beginning again on a new continent.
recaps.in_short: Jamie Fraser survives Culloden, spends years hiding as an outlaw on his own land, then seven more in Ardsmuir prison, and is finally paroled to an English estate where a coerced night with the daughter of the house leaves him a son he can never acknowledge. In 1968 Claire, Brianna and Roger trace him through the records and find proof that he is alive in Edinburgh twenty years on, printing seditious pamphlets under an assumed name. Claire goes back through the stones and finds him. Their reunion is immediately complicated: Jamie is a smuggler with a burned print shop, a runaway nephew, and a wife in the Highlands he never mentioned. When Young Ian is carried off by pirates, the Frasers follow him across the Atlantic aboard a ship bound for the West Indies, through a typhoid epidemic, a shipwreck and a Jamaican governor's ball, to a confrontation with Geillis Duncan, who is alive and means to use the boy in a passage through the stones. Claire kills her; a hurricane then wrecks their ship and casts them ashore in the American colonies.

recaps.text: Previously, in Outlander and Dragonfly in Amber: Claire Randall, a wartime nurse, was carried from 1945 to 1743 through the standing stones at Craigh na Dun. Compelled to marry the outlawed Highlander Jamie Fraser to escape an English officer, Captain Jonathan Randall, she came to love him and chose to stay in the past. Knowing that the Jacobite rising of 1745 would end in the destruction of the Highlands, the two spent two years in France trying to stop Charles Stuart before he could sail, at the cost of a stillborn daughter and Jamie's imprisonment. The rising happened anyway. They rode out with it, saw the early victory at Prestonpans and the long retreat that followed, and on the eve of Culloden Jamie killed his kinsman Dougal MacKenzie to protect Claire, then sent her back through the stones pregnant with their second child, intending to die in the battle. Claire returned to 1948 and to her first husband, Frank Randall, who raised her daughter Brianna as his own. In 1968, two years after Frank's death, Claire told Brianna the truth, and the historian Roger Wakefield found a record showing that Jamie Fraser did not die at Culloden.

Jamie wakes on the field at Culloden among the dead, his leg wounded, with Jonathan Randall's body lying across him; Randall died in the battle. Highlanders who can still walk carry the wounded to a farmhouse, where English officers work through the survivors shooting them in turn. Jamie's name comes up before Lord Melton, an English officer whose brother owes Jamie a debt of honour, and Melton refuses to execute him. Rather than take him prisoner, he has Jamie loaded into a wagon and sent home to Lallybroch to die there. Meanwhile, in 1948, Claire arrives back in her own century pregnant and destroyed by grief. Frank takes her back and offers to raise the child as his, on terms: she will not speak of the past, she will not look for Jamie Fraser, and the child will be his daughter. They leave England for a new post in Boston.

Jamie does not die. He recovers at Lallybroch and, since the estate is under constant threat from patrolling redcoats, spends years hiding in a cave on his own hillside, a hunted man the tenants call the Dunbonnet. His sister Jenny feeds him, his family shields him, and the whole district lies to the English for him. Life at Lallybroch grinds on under occupation, hunger, and the punitive laws that follow the rising, and Jenny bears another son. When there is nothing left to hold together and the estate is desperate for money, Jamie has himself betrayed and taken by the English so that his family can claim the reward on his head, on the understanding that he will be imprisoned rather than hanged.

Jamie is held for years at Ardsmuir, an isolated Scottish prison where he becomes the spokesman for the Jacobite inmates. The new governor, Lord John Grey, is a young English officer who has met Jamie once before and has reason to feel humiliated by it; he gives Jamie parole, chess and conversation, and finds his feelings running further than he intends. A wandering madman brought in from the moors dies muttering about a white witch and a cache of French gold, and Jamie escapes briefly to follow it, which gives Grey the leverage to keep him under closer control. When Ardsmuir is closed and its prisoners are transported to the American colonies as indentured labour, Grey quietly arranges instead for Jamie to be paroled to an English estate in the Lake District. In 1968, Claire, Brianna and Roger comb through prison rolls and ledgers trying to follow him, while Brianna struggles to accept what her mother has told her.

At Helwater, Jamie works as a groom under a false name, forbidden to leave the estate. Geneva Dunsany, the elder daughter of the house, discovers his real identity and blackmails him into her bed on the eve of her marriage to a rich old earl. She dies giving birth to a son, and the circumstances of the earl's own death leave the boy heir to the title. Jamie, who cannot claim the child without ruining him, stays on as a servant to be near him and teaches him to ride. Lord John Grey marries Geneva's sister Isobel and takes on the family, promising to see the boy raised well. When the resemblance between groom and heir becomes impossible to ignore, Jamie leaves. In 1968 the search stalls and starts again, and Claire faces the question of what she would do if Jamie were ever actually found.

Roger finds it: a seditious pamphlet and a printer's imprint that place a Scottish printer named Alexander Malcolm in Edinburgh in 1766, twenty years after Culloden, with a description and a history that can only belong to Jamie Fraser. Claire has to decide whether to leave her life, her career and her grown daughter to go back to a man who has lived two decades she knows nothing about. Brianna, who has come to accept the story, tells her to go. Claire settles her affairs in Boston, has clothes made to suit the period, packs medicines and instruments, and says goodbye to her daughter and to Roger. She goes to Craigh na Dun and steps into the stones.

Claire finds the print shop in Edinburgh and walks in on Jamie, who faints at the sight of her. The reunion is joyful and then complicated. Jamie lodges in a brothel, prints treasonous pamphlets, and finances everything by smuggling French brandy, with the one-handed Fergus grown up and running errands, a Chinese exile called Mr. Willoughby in tow, and his fourteen-year-old nephew Young Ian hiding in the city rather than going home to Jenny. Excise men and a corrupt official circle the business. The print shop is burned down during a fight in which Young Ian kills a man who was searching it. Worse, Claire learns from Ian what Jamie never told her: after Ardsmuir he married Laoghaire MacKenzie, and the marriage still stands. Jamie takes them all out of Edinburgh on a smuggling run to the coast.

They go home to Lallybroch, where Claire is met with delight by some of the family and cold anger by others, and where Laoghaire soon arrives to claim her husband. In the confrontation that follows Claire leaves, and Laoghaire shoots Jamie; Claire comes back to treat the wound and the two of them finally have out everything the twenty years have left unsaid. A lawyer establishes that Jamie owes Laoghaire a settlement he cannot possibly pay, which sends him after a cache of treasure hidden on a small island off the coast, left there years earlier and known to almost nobody. Young Ian, the only strong swimmer, dives for it and brings it up, and is seized on the beach by the crew of a pirate ship, which sails with him aboard.

Jamie's cousin Jared provides a ship, the Artemis, and the Frasers sail for the West Indies after the pirates, guessing that the boy will be sold there. Claire signs on as surgeon; Fergus and Marsali, Laoghaire's elder daughter, have stowed away together and intend to marry, which Jamie forbids until a priest can be found. Jamie is violently seasick for most of the crossing and manages it with acupuncture from Mr. Willoughby, who finally tells the story of how a Chinese scholar came to be a drunk in Edinburgh. The crew is superstitious, the winds are contrary, and the trail of the pirate ship is thin, but a Scottish sailor's account and a merchant's records keep them following it westward across the Atlantic.

A British warship hails the Artemis: typhoid has killed most of her officers, and her acting captain presses Claire aboard to fight the epidemic. She saves what men she can, then discovers that the captain has identified Jamie as a wanted traitor and a murderer and intends to arrest him in Jamaica. Rather than be carried there, Claire goes over the side off the coast of Hispaniola and reaches shore, where an eccentric priest living in the hills gives her food and shelter. The Artemis, blown off course by a storm and beached for repairs, turns out to be on the same stretch of coast, and Claire and Jamie find each other again. With the ship refitted and the priest willing to officiate, Fergus and Marsali are married.

In Jamaica the Frasers move carefully, wanted men in a small colony. Slave markets and plantation gossip put them on the track of a boy answering Young Ian's description, sold to a wealthy estate owner, and they buy a slave named Ishmael who has been inside that household. Invited to the new governor's ball, Jamie and Claire find that the governor is Lord John Grey, an old friend of Jamie's from his prison years, whose arrival is both a comfort and a danger given the warrants out against them. At the same reception Claire recognises another guest: Geillis Duncan, the woman she watched condemned as a witch twenty years earlier, alive, wealthy, married under another name, and buying up gemstones.

Geillis has Young Ian, and her interest in him is not casual. She has spent years assembling the stones she believes a traveller needs, has worked out a prophecy about a Scottish king, and means to go forward through a passage in a cave called Abandawe, using the boy as the blood price she thinks the crossing demands. Claire follows her into the cave, where the sound of the passage is overwhelming, and kills her. Ian is freed and the party escapes. In Jamaica, Lord John has also brought out the boy Jamie fathered at Helwater, and Claire finally sees for herself the son Jamie has never been able to claim. With warrants out against them for murder and piracy, the Frasers cannot remain in Jamaica and put to sea, and the ship is caught and broken by a hurricane. Claire and Jamie are washed up alive on the coast of Georgia, in the American colonies, with Young Ian and a handful of survivors, no money, no ship, and no intention of going back. They begin again there.

characters.description: A young girl living in Puerto Rico who keeps a journal. She is bright, watchful and given to blunt observations about the adults around her, and she has dreams and impressions she cannot account for, which her family treats as an overactive imagination. She is the first voice in the book, and nothing in her life appears to connect her to the giant machine the world has been watching for a decade.
characters.name: Eva Reyes

characters.description: A BBC reporter in London who is on air when an enormous figure appears overnight in the middle of the city, standing motionless in a park and answering nothing. His broadcasts are the public record of the standoff as it develops, and he reports it from close range while the authorities are still deciding what it is.
characters.name: Jacob Lawson

characters.description: Head of the science division of the Earth Defense Corps, the international body that now operates Themis, and the physicist who has understood the machine better than anyone since she fell into its hand as a child. She is also, by her own account, a copy: the Rose Franklin who ran the original project died, and this one appeared afterwards carrying her memories and no explanation for herself. She works constantly, partly because the work is urgent and partly because it is easier than the question of what she is.
characters.name: Rose Franklin

characters.description: A brigadier general and the commanding officer of the Earth Defense Corps. Dry, plainspoken and unimpressed by ceremony, he spends more of his time managing the governments that fund him than the people who work for him. He is protective of his staff, blunt with his superiors, and skeptical of any plan whose first step is to fire something.
characters.name: Eugene Govender

characters.description: A captain in the Earth Defense Corps and one of Themis's two pilots, a former army helicopter pilot who has spent a decade inside the machine. Direct to the point of rudeness, contemptuous of the public appearances the job now involves, and closer to Vincent Couture than to anyone else, though a decade of the same work in the same confined space has worn at both of them.
characters.name: Kara Resnik

characters.description: A man interviewed without any stated occupation, who is evidently well informed about the machine, its history and the people around it, and who has access no ordinary official would have. He speaks carefully, volunteers little, and is plainly acting for interests he declines to name.
characters.name: Mr. Burns

characters.description: Themis's other pilot and the Earth Defense Corps' consultant on the machine's language and controls, the Montreal linguist who first read its script. Sardonic, quick with a joke at the wrong moment, and by now more soldier than academic. He has been with Kara Resnik for years and is handling the accumulated strain of the decade less well than he lets on.
characters.name: Vincent Couture

characters.description: A security guard at the Earth Defense Corps who once flew with Kara Resnik and followed her into the project. He has stayed near her for years in a post well below what he trained for, and his feelings for her have not changed in that time.
characters.name: Ryan Mitchell

characters.description: A lieutenant general commanding Joint Special Operations Command, brought into the crisis as it escalates. He treats the situation as a military problem with a military answer, has little patience for the Earth Defense Corps' insistence on studying before acting, and represents the governments that would prefer the matter settled with weapons.
characters.name: Alan A. Simms

characters.description: The Earth Defense Corps' geneticist, who has spent years on the markers that determine who can pilot Themis. Exacting, driven and socially isolated, with a stammer she dislikes having noticed, she is widely disliked by her colleagues and has never been given the standing she believes her work deserves.
characters.name: Alyssa Papantoniou

recaps.ending: The attack is brought to an end, but not as a victory. Themis, piloted by Vincent Couture and his ten-year-old daughter Eva Reyes, is used against the visitors' machines in the final confrontation. By then the substance released in the world's cities has killed on the order of a hundred million people, whole districts of major capitals are dead ground, and humanity has learned that part of its own population descends from the people who sent the machines. Kara Resnik does not survive the book; she is killed before the end, and the letter she leaves for Vincent is read after her death. What follows the fighting is a judgement rather than a settlement: Rose Franklin, Vincent and Eva are taken off Earth altogether, along with Themis, by the people who built it. Eugene Govender, Ryan Mitchell and the rest of the Earth Defense Corps are left behind on a planet permanently altered by what has happened, without the machine and without the three people who understood it best. Rose, Vincent and Eva arrive on a world that is not theirs, with no way home, no idea how long they will be kept there, and no assurance that Earth's reprieve is permanent.
recaps.in_short: Ten years after Themis was assembled, it is operated publicly by the Earth Defense Corps, with Rose Franklin heading its science division and Kara Resnik and Vincent Couture as its pilots. Then a second giant machine appears overnight in London and stands silent for days before releasing a substance that kills everyone for miles around. More of them appear in cities across the world and do the same, and the dead are counted in the tens of millions and then far higher. Rose works out why they have come, and the answer turns on ancestry: some humans carry the visitors' genetic inheritance, which is also what decides who can pilot. A girl in Puerto Rico, Eva Reyes, proves to be the biological daughter of Kara and Vincent, conceived without their knowledge by the project's geneticist. Kara is killed, and Vincent trains his daughter to pilot Themis with him. The confrontation ends the attack at a cost of roughly a hundred million lives, and Rose, Vincent and Eva are taken off Earth by the machines' builders, along with Themis.

recaps.text: Previously: as a child, Rose Franklin fell through the ground outside Deadwood, South Dakota and landed in the palm of a giant metal hand buried in a lighted chamber. As an adult she led the research into it, funded and directed by an unnamed man of unexplained wealth and influence. The remaining pieces were located by the interference they caused in electronics and magnetic readings, and were recovered from sites around the world. The assembled figure, roughly two hundred feet tall and made of an alloy nothing on Earth can produce, was named Themis. It is operated by two people standing in a control room inside it, whose movements it copies, and the controls answer to only a small number of humans, who were found to carry genetic sequences the rest of the population does not: whoever left the machine on Earth also left descendants here. Kara Resnik, a United States Army helicopter pilot, and Vincent Couture, a linguist from Montreal, became its pilots and its couple. Rose was killed during the project and was replaced by a woman identical to her, who remembers being Rose and cannot explain where she came from. Ryan Mitchell, who flew with Kara before the project, stayed close to her; the geneticist Alyssa Papantoniou ran the work on the markers. By the end of the first book Themis was whole, publicly known and used, and switching it on had effectively announced to its builders that humans had found their machine.

Ten years on, Themis is a public institution. It is operated by the Earth Defense Corps under Brigadier General Eugene Govender, with Rose Franklin heading the science division and Kara Resnik and Vincent Couture still its only pilots, doing demonstrations and appearances as much as anything else. Then a second giant appears overnight in the middle of London, standing in a park: the same kind of machine as Themis, but not Themis. It does nothing at all. It does not respond to contact, broadcast or approach, and no government can establish what it is waiting for. Crowds gather to look at it, parts of the city empty and other parts fill, and the world's governments argue over whether to negotiate with it, evacuate around it or attack it. Themis is sent to London to stand in front of it, partly as a show of force and partly because Rose wants to know whether the two machines register each other at all. Rose's own attention is on what the arrival implies: if this one came, it came from whoever built Themis, and it did not travel that far to be photographed.

The machine in London kills. Without warning or demand it releases a substance into the air that kills everyone within miles of it, and the centre of the city is emptied of the living in minutes. Themis is present and can do nothing useful about it. The dead are counted first in the tens of thousands and then far higher, and the survivors are the people who happened to be outside the radius or shielded from it. In the days that follow, more of the same machines appear in cities across several continents, each standing silent where it lands, and the world waits to learn whether every one of them will do what the first one did. Governments demand an immediate military response; the Earth Defense Corps argues that nobody yet understands what they are dealing with. Rose Franklin works on what the substance is, how it disperses and whether anything can be done to counter it. Meanwhile a girl in Puerto Rico, Eva Reyes, is behaving in ways her family cannot explain, and she comes to the attention of people who have been keeping records about exactly that kind of thing.

Eva Reyes turns out to be the biological daughter of Kara Resnik and Vincent Couture, conceived without their knowledge or consent from material taken during the project's medical screening and carried to term by another woman. Alyssa Papantoniou arranged it years earlier, as an experiment in whether the ability to pilot could be inherited and concentrated. The revelation lands on Kara and Vincent in the middle of a global emergency, and on a child who has to be told what she is and why it matters. Militarily, nothing works: conventional strikes on the machines fail, and every attempt risks provoking another release. Rose Franklin's work turns from what the substance does to why the visitors are doing it at all, and the answer keeps returning to the same genetic inheritance that decides who can operate Themis. The worldwide death toll climbs into the tens of millions and keeps rising as more machines act. Jacob Lawson, who was reporting from London when its machine released the substance, is among the survivors and describes what the attack looked like from inside it.

Kara Resnik is killed. Themis is left with one pilot and no obvious replacement, because the number of people the controls will answer to is very small and Eva Reyes, ten years old, is one of them. Vincent Couture begins training with his daughter, which is the only option available and which nobody involved is comfortable with, least of all him. Kara leaves a letter for Vincent that he reads afterwards. Govender takes the situation to the United Nations General Assembly, because the machines are no longer a British or an American problem and the Earth Defense Corps cannot act without agreement it does not have. Rose Franklin's conclusions harden: the visitors came because of the ancestry a portion of humanity carries, an inheritance that should not exist and that the builders of these machines did not intend to leave behind. Monitoring stations begin registering activity that suggests the situation is about to change again, and the Corps starts planning for the possibility that the machines will not simply keep standing where they are.

With the machines still standing in the world's cities and the death toll rising each time one of them acts, the remaining options are all bad ones. Nuclear release is openly under discussion and the assets to carry it out are moved into position. Vincent Couture and Eva Reyes have trained far enough to operate Themis together, although Eva is a child and the physical demands of the controls were never designed with one in mind. Rose Franklin settles on a course of action based on what she now believes the visitors want rather than on anything a military plan can deliver, and it requires Themis to be used in a way that will not be forgiven if she has misread them. The Earth Defense Corps commits to her plan over the objections of the governments that would rather see the machines bombed, and Govender spends what authority he has left to make it happen.

Themis, piloted by Vincent Couture and his daughter Eva Reyes, is used against the visitors' machines, and the confrontation brings the attack to an end. The cost is enormous. The substance released in the world's cities has killed on the order of a hundred million people, whole districts of major capitals are dead ground, and humanity now knows that part of its own population descends from the people who sent the machines, a fact that will shape everything that comes afterwards. Kara Resnik is dead. What follows the fighting is not a victory but a judgement: Rose Franklin, Vincent and Eva are taken off Earth altogether, along with Themis, by the people who built it. Eugene Govender, Ryan Mitchell and the rest of the Earth Defense Corps are left behind with a changed planet, no machine and none of the three people who understood it best. Rose, Vincent and Eva arrive on a world that is not theirs, with no way home and no idea how long they will be held there.

characters.description: An old pagan Northumbrian lord, master of the sword Serpent-Breath, and by common repute the most famous warrior in Britain. He has outlived nearly every king he served and holds the great fortress on its rock above the sea that he spent a lifetime winning back. He wants only to be left in peace there, and two things prevent it: he is sworn to Guthfrith, the Norse king of Northumbria, whom he despises, and he made Aethelstan, the Saxon king ruling everything to the south, who swore in return that he would never invade Northumbria while Uhtred lived.
characters.name: Uhtred of Bebbanburg

characters.description: The Irish swordsman who has fought beside Uhtred for a lifetime: his second in command, his closest friend, and the man he trusts to tell him when he is being a fool.
characters.name: Finan

characters.description: The Italian-born woman who came north with Uhtred after the fighting for Lundene, carried away from her own country by slavers as a child. She shares his hall at Bebbanburg, speaks to him more bluntly than anyone but Finan dares, and has no patience at all with Saxon kings.
characters.name: Benedetta

characters.description: Alfred's grandson: the king Uhtred raised, taught and twice put on his throne, now ruler of Wessex, Mercia and East Anglia and the most powerful man in Britain. Devoutly Christian and increasingly certain that God means him to rule the whole island, he is no longer the young man who needed Uhtred's protection, and the oath he swore to leave Northumbria alone sits badly with his ambition.
characters.name: Aethelstan

characters.description: The Norse king of Northumbria, brother of the dead Sigtryggr, and Uhtred's nominal lord. Drunken, cruel and distrusted by the men who are supposed to follow him, he holds the last kingdom in Britain outside Saxon rule and has neither the wit nor the loyalty to keep it.
characters.name: Guthfrith

characters.description: Uhtred's son and heir, a capable warrior who commands men at Bebbanburg and will hold the fortress after his father. He carries the same name, as every lord of Bebbanburg does.
characters.name: Uhtred the Younger

characters.description: A Norse warrior and poet who holds land from Uhtred on the northern border. Formidable in a fight, cheerfully irreligious, and one of the few neighbours whose company Uhtred actively enjoys.
characters.name: Egil Skallagrimmrson

characters.description: A Norse lord who has taken the Christian faith and become the man King Aethelstan trusts and favours above everyone else. Handsome, fervent in his new religion and persuasive at court, he holds land in the north-west and speaks with the king's voice. Uhtred distrusts him from their first meeting and cannot justify it beyond instinct.
characters.name: Ingilmundr

characters.description: A young, ambitious West Saxon sent north with the king's authority over Northumbrian lands. Contemptuous of the old lord of Bebbanburg and open about what he thinks the fortress is worth, he has Aethelstan's warrant and intends to use it.
characters.name: Ealdred

characters.description: A bishop in Aethelstan's service, Danish by descent and Saxon by loyalty, and one of the shrewdest men at the king's court. He carries the king's demands to Uhtred and is honest with him about what they mean, which makes him the nearest thing to a friend Uhtred has among Aethelstan's churchmen.
characters.name: Oda

characters.description: The Norse king of Dublin: an ambitious and capable war leader with a fleet, a family claim to Northumbria, and the intention of taking back everything the Norse have lost in Britain. He is willing to make an ally of every enemy Aethelstan has.
characters.name: Anlaf

characters.description: King of Alba and the most dangerous ruler in the north, an old rival who has spent years testing Northumbria's borders. Made to acknowledge Aethelstan as his overlord, he has no intention of remaining anyone's client king.
characters.name: Constantine

characters.description: King of Strath Clota, whose lands lie between the Scots and the Norse of the Irish Sea. Another ruler forced to bow to Aethelstan's overlordship, and another who brings his army against him when the chance comes.
characters.name: Owain

recaps.ending: The alliance is destroyed at Brunanburh. After a day of shield wall against shield wall the Saxon line holds and then breaks the enemy, and the Norse and Scottish army is slaughtered as it runs. Constantine loses his son, the northern kings' strength is broken, and Anlaf escapes with what is left of his fleet back to Ireland. Ingilmundr, the favourite Aethelstan trusted and loved above everyone, is revealed to have been the enemy's man, a betrayal that costs the king more privately than the battle cost him in warriors. Aethelstan is left the undisputed ruler of all the English and overlord of Britain, and the victory becomes the thing his name is remembered for. Uhtred, who fought for the north rather than for the king, comes out of it alive and with what he wanted: Bebbanburg is his, Ealdred's claim on it is finished, and a king who has broken one oath is in no position to break another. He rides home with Finan to Benedetta and his family, an old man who has fought his last battle, and takes up again the only thing he ever truly wanted - the fortress above the sea, and the prospect of dying in his own hall rather than in a shield wall. The series ends with him there, alive, holding the place he spent a lifetime taking back.
recaps.in_short: Aethelstan, the king Uhtred made, breaks the oath he swore, invades Northumbria and takes the last kingdom in Britain outside Saxon rule, forcing its lords - Uhtred among them - and the kings of the Scots, the Strathclyde Britons and the Welsh to accept him as overlord. Uhtred, old and wanting only peace, is squeezed by the king's new favourites: the Norse convert Ingilmundr, whom Aethelstan trusts above anyone, and the ambitious Ealdred, who covets Bebbanburg and seizes the fortress while Uhtred is away. Uhtred takes it back by trickery. Meanwhile Anlaf, the Norse king of Dublin, assembles a great alliance of Scots, Strathclyde Britons and the Norse of Ireland and Northumbria to destroy Aethelstan and divide his kingdoms, and offers Uhtred a crown to join it or stand aside. Uhtred chooses against the invaders. The armies meet at Brunanburh, where a day-long slaughter ends with the alliance broken, Constantine's son dead and Anlaf fleeing to his ships. Aethelstan is left ruler of all the English; Uhtred survives, keeps Bebbanburg, and goes home to the sea.

recaps.text: Earlier in the series: Uhtred of Bebbanburg, born to a Northumbrian lord, raised by Danes and pagan all his life, spent forty years as the sword of the Christian kings of Wessex and Mercia - Alfred, then Alfred's son Edward and daughter Aethelflaed - while never losing sight of his real purpose: Bebbanburg, the sea fortress stolen from him as a boy, which he finally took back by storm. He also raised, taught and repeatedly saved Alfred's grandson Aethelstan, whose enemies called him a bastard to keep him from the throne. When Edward died, Uhtred was dragged into the succession war, endured captivity at the hands of a brutal enemy champion, and saw Aethelstan's rivals destroyed at Lundene. Aethelstan was crowned king of Wessex, Mercia and East Anglia, the mightiest ruler in Britain, and swore to Uhtred that he would never invade Northumbria while Uhtred lived. Northumbria, the last kingdom outside Saxon rule, had been held by Uhtred's son-in-law Sigtryggr; since Sigtryggr's death it has passed to his brother Guthfrith, a drunkard Uhtred despises and is nonetheless sworn to. Uhtred is old now, wants no more wars, and has Finan, Benedetta and his family around him in the fortress above the sea.

So far: Aethelstan breaks his oath. He marches an army north, takes Northumbria for himself, and Guthfrith's kingship collapses; the king flees his own country rather than face the Saxons. Uhtred, who wanted no part of any of it, finds his lands inside a Saxon realm for the first time in his life. Aethelstan then summons the rulers of Britain to acknowledge him as their overlord, and one by one they do it - Constantine of Alba, Owain of Strath Clota, the kings of Wales - and Uhtred, the man who put Aethelstan on his throne, is required to swear with the rest. The king receiving those oaths is not the young man Uhtred taught: he is imperious, convinced that God intends him to rule the whole island, and surrounded by new favourites. Two of them matter. Ingilmundr is a Norse lord turned devout Christian, the man Aethelstan trusts and loves above all others, and whom Uhtred mistrusts on sight without being able to say why. Ealdred is a young West Saxon given authority over the north, contemptuous of Uhtred and open about how much he would like Bebbanburg for himself. Uhtred goes home understanding that his peace is over and that the king's men will not leave his fortress alone.

So far: The king's men take what they want. Drawn away from home, Uhtred loses Bebbanburg to Ealdred, who occupies it with the king's warrant while the garrison has no orders that would let it resist, and Guthfrith's flight ends with the deposed king dead. Landless, with only his household warriors and the help of his neighbour Egil Skallagrimmrson, Uhtred does not attempt a siege he could never win: he takes his fortress back by a trick, which restores his home and puts him in open defiance of Aethelstan's authority. While the Saxons quarrel over the north, a far larger danger gathers in the west. Anlaf, the Norse king of Dublin, has built an alliance to break Aethelstan and carve up his kingdoms - the Norse of Ireland and of Northumbria, Constantine and the Scots, Owain of Strath Clota, all of them men who knelt to the Saxon king and resented it. Anlaf seeks Uhtred out and makes him an offer: Northumbria, and a crown, if he joins the invasion or simply keeps his men at home. Uhtred has every reason to hate Aethelstan by now, and the choice is genuinely open - an old man with a fortress to protect, working out which oath still binds him and which side would leave the north standing.

So far: The invasion comes. Anlaf's fleets land, his allies march, and Aethelstan calls out the levies of all his kingdoms. Uhtred makes his choice: whatever he owes Aethelstan personally, he will not stand aside while a Norse and Scottish army takes Northumbria, and he brings his men to the muster with Finan and Egil beside him. What he carries with him is worth more than the numbers he adds, because he has met Anlaf and knows something of how the alliance means to fight.
